clauses.reason: Whole withdrawal revoked by EO 8861 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, August 20, 1941): 'Executive Orders No. 4109 of December 8, 1924, No. 4262 of July 3, 1925, and No. 4430 of April 23, 1926 ... are hereby revoked'. EO 8861 states no effective date; recorded as effective on signing, 1941-08-20 (the alternative reading, effect on Federal Register publication at 6 FR 4289 on August 22, 1941, is disclosed). Earlier events each ended the withdrawal only for the lands they name: EO 4372 (1926-01-23, Batton Islands and Key Biscayne), EO 4485 (1926-07-24, part of Amelia Island); EO 7993 (1938-10-27, Great White Heron Refuge lands) and EO 8508 (1940-08-08, 195.26 acres in T. 3 S., R. 31 W.) did the same and are disclosed in the rationale. EO 8725 (1941-03-29) took precedence over EO 4109 for its gunnery-range lands but expressly did not rescind or revoke it, so it ended no part. Actor of the end: EO 8861.

research_rationale:
EO 4109 (December 8, 1924, Calvin Coolidge), read in full in the held ProQuest replica scan (archival_replica_scan_pending_codebook, acceptable_as_original false) and checked against the page image rendered from the held PDF (ProQuest Pre-1937 Orders/PT1-1924-EO-4109.pdf, sha256 e75a8313...; one page; heading 'Executive Order', 'FLORIDA', signature 'CALVIN COOLIDGE', 'The White House, December 8, 1924', '[No. 4109]'; Interior received stamp December 18, 1924; State Department true-copy date December 17, 1924). The OCR layer holds every printed line of the order; its errors ('Executve odber', 'the. same', stamp noise) do not touch the operative words. One operative command: under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847) as amended August 24, 1912 (37 Stat. 497), 'all islands belonging to the United States in Florida situated in the waters off the coast or in the coastal waters of the State' are withdrawn from settlement, location, sale, entry and all forms of appropriation, subject to valid existing rights, 'for classification and in aid of legislation'. No stated effective date; effective on signing. The order states no term and no own-terms end: its purpose (classification and legislation) is not shown to have been completed, and completion would not itself have ended a withdrawal that runs until revoked. First and whole end: EO 8861 (Franklin D. Roosevelt, August 20, 1941), held as an APP mirror transcription (page record checked: MIRROR_DOCUMENTS row heading names EO 8861 and Nos. 4109, 4262 and 4430, date 1941-08-20, text_sha256 equals the held text) and in the held Federal Register text of 6 FR 4289 (August 22, 1941; F.R. Doc. 41-6244, filed August 21, 1941): the three orders 'are hereby revoked, the lands thus released becoming subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'. EO 8861 states no effective date; recorded as 1941-08-20, the signing date, with publication on August 22, 1941 as the disclosed alternative. Partial later events cited: EO 4372 (January 23, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) revoked EO 4109 as to the abandoned military reservations on Batton Islands and Key Biscayne; EO 4485 (July 24, 1926; ProQuest scan, page image checked) as to fractional sec. 6, T. 1 N., R. 29 E., on Amelia Island; EO 8725 (March 29, 1941; aerial gunnery ranges; held Federal Register text) 'shall take precedence over but shall not rescind or revoke' EO 4109 for its lands, recorded as a later event that ended nothing. Two further partial events are held but disclosed rather than cited, because the dossier offers them only as APP transcriptions while official Federal Register copies are held (jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_7993.txt and EO_8508.txt) and the working-text gate refuses a transcription when an official copy exists: EO 7993 (October 27, 1938; Great White Heron Refuge) superseded EO 4109 'insofar as such withdrawals affect the above-described lands', and EO 8508 (August 8, 1940; antiaircraft firing range, 195.26 acres in T. 3 S., R. 31 W.) superseded it 'as to any of the above-described lands'. Each released only named lands before the whole revocation, so neither changes the first end or the status. The 1989 OFR codification disposition table (held: jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/DISPOSITION_1989.csv) lists EO 4109 as 'Amended by EOs 4372, 4485, 7993, 8508' and 'Revoked by EO 8861', which matches this inventory of events. Contrary evidence checked: the dossier's actor records for EOs 8858, 8859 and 8860 come from the same Federal Register pages (6 FR 4288-4289) as EO 8861 and are page-neighbour artefacts; the held FR texts of EOs 7994, 8509, 8510 and 8724 that mention EO 4109 are the same pages as EOs 7993, 8508 and 8725; a citation search of every held order text found no instrument after August 20, 1941 that names EO 4109.

savings.reason: EO 8861 contains no savings clause. The lands it released became 'subject to the provisions of Executive Order No. 6964 of February 5, 1935'; that continuing withdrawal is EO 6964's own command and belongs to its lifecycle, not a residual of EO 4109. Valid existing rights were excepted from the withdrawal from the start and were never affected by it. Lands reserved by EOs 7993 and 8508 continued under those orders, not under EO 4109.
